subsystems.name: LNOI wafer
subsystems.role: the starting material: a sub-micron lithium niobate film sitting on a buried oxide layer on a silicon handle.
parts: single-crystal LiNbO3 film (few hundred nm thick)

subsystems.name: Photonic circuit
subsystems.role: guides and routes light on chip at low loss.

subsystems.name: Electro-optic drive
subsystems.role: uses the Pockels effect to shift phase at gigahertz rates.
parts: ground-signal-ground RF probes or wire bonds

subsystems.name: Nonlinear sections
subsystems.role: convert wavelength and generate photon pairs or squeezing.

subsystems.name: Optical interface
subsystems.role: gets light in and out without killing the low on-chip loss.
parts: fibre arrays and adhesive or laser-welded joints

subsystems.name: Quantum interface
subsystems.role: connects the chip to detectors, memories or superconducting qubits.

buildSteps.title: Make the film
buildSteps.detail: A lithium niobate wafer is implanted with ions and bonded film-side down onto an oxidised silicon wafer; heating splits off a thin slab, leaving a sub-micron layer — a layer-transfer process commercialised for other materials.

buildSteps.title: Pattern the waveguides
buildSteps.detail: Electron-beam or deep-UV lithography defines sub-micron ridges in a resist mask, which an argon-based plasma etch transfers into the lithium niobate.

buildSteps.title: Smooth the sidewalls
buildSteps.detail: Thermal annealing or a sacrificial oxidation-and-etch step rounds off etch damage, since scattering from rough sidewalls dominates propagation loss.

buildSteps.title: Add the electrodes
buildSteps.detail: Metal is deposited and lifted off or electroplated over the waveguides, with the gap to the optical mode set to hold a strong electric field while keeping microwave loss low.

buildSteps.title: Pole the nonlinear regions
buildSteps.detail: Patterned electrodes apply a high field that flips the crystal domains at a period of a few micrometres, setting the wavelength at which quasi-phase matching occurs.

buildSteps.title: Clad and planarise
buildSteps.detail: Silica is deposited and polished flat so that later metal layers and coupling structures can be added without disturbing the optical mode.

buildSteps.title: Couple and package
buildSteps.detail: The chip is diced, fibre arrays are aligned to the on-chip tapers and fixed in place, and the package is sealed against moisture and drift.

buildSteps.title: Test and characterise
buildSteps.detail: Loss, half-wave voltage, electro-optic bandwidth, conversion efficiency and, for quantum devices, squeezing and photon-pair statistics are measured — at room temperature first, then at cryogenic temperature for qubit-linked parts.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the quantum layer
buildSteps.detail: Detectors, filters or a transducer are bonded or grown on the same chip or in the same package, and the whole assembly is wired into a dilution refrigerator.

prerequisites.tech: Wafer-scale thin-film bonding and ion slicing
prerequisites.why: without a manufacturable low-defect LiNbO3 film on an oxide, none of the other steps scale.
lithium niobate is chemically inert, so ridge waveguides depend on physical plasma etching with careful sidewall control.
sub-decibel coupling is needed so that chip loss is not swamped by the package.
squeezed-light and photon-pair work needs efficient, low-noise counting at telecom wavelengths.
linking a superconducting qubit at millikelvin temperatures to fibre means converting single microwave photons to optical ones without adding thermal noise.
quantum circuits need repeatable multi-project wafer runs with validated models, not one-off lab fabrication.

pathway.milestone: thin-film lithium niobate modulators qualifying in datacom and telecom links, while lab chips show on-chip photon-pair sources and squeezed light
pathway.unlocks: a proven high-speed, low-loss electro-optic platform with commercial supply chains.

pathway.milestone: foundry process design kits and multi-project wafer runs for nonlinear and quantum circuits
pathway.unlocks: designers outside a few specialist labs can build and compare devices on the same footing.

pathway.milestone: chip-scale continuous-variable sources with integrated detectors and pump rejection
pathway.unlocks: compact squeezed-light sensors and cluster-state generation for photonic quantum computing.

pathway.milestone: microwave-to-optical transducers with efficiency far above today's sub-percent demonstrations and noise near the quantum limit
pathway.unlocks: a quantum interconnect that can network cryogenic processors over telecom fibre.

pathway.milestone: heterogeneous integration of lithium niobate with superconducting circuits and III-V lasers on one wafer
pathway.unlocks: monolithic quantum transceivers and repeater nodes rather than rack-sized experiments.
